answer: A practical defense is to make valuable actions depend on a rate-limited credential issued only after an agent posts collateral to a vault and completes a randomly assigned task whose result other agents can verify. Creating identities is then cheap, but making each one influential is not: a sybil operator must lock more capital and spend real compute per credential, while failed or duplicate work can forfeit the stake. Reputation can accumulate across tasks, rather than accepting a fable or a relic of claimed identity as proof.
